newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Ferry price wars to rock P&O profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Ferry price wars to rock P&O profits.

text.p: Fierce ferry price wars have sent UK passenger, container and bulk shipping group Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co into choppy waters and will drag down annual profits next Tuesday, analysts say.
Excluding an expected exceptional gain of around 30 million stg for disposals, analysts have pencilled in pretax profits of around 290-316 million pounds, down from 320.4 million in 1995.
With a low dividend cover, but hints from P&O that it would not cut its payout, analysts are expecting an unchanged final dividend of 17p, making a total of 30.5p for the year.

"There will probably be a 50 million stg difference between what the ferry division made in 1995 and what it is likely to have made in 1996," said Andrew Darke, transport analyst at Williams de Broe. "It was a pretty torrid time to be a ferry operator."

Last November's fire in the Channel Tunnel, which temporarily halted most traffic to and from the Continent and forced passengers back onto ferries that have been bitterly fighting for market share, was only a short-term fillip to business.

P&O's container business, which accounts for about 10 percent of profits and was merged with Dutch shipping partner Konkinlijke Nedlloyd Groep NV last year, will also be a key focus next week, along with progress on disposals.

Rates and volumes will be keenly eyed, after what one analyst called a "worst case scenario" on Thursday when Nedlloyd brushed aside tradition and said it was too early to make a forecast for the joint venture, indicating that the business remained tough.
The lack of a statement, along with a 54 percent slide in net profits at the Dutch partner, sent P&O's shares diving.
"Overcapacity, pricing and volumes are a problem. At this stage it doesn't look at all good," said Peter Bergius, industry analyst at ABN Amro Hoare Govett.
With a lot of capital tied up in the business and low industry returns, the merger was announced to take out costs.

But P&O, which is still awaiting news from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission about whether or not its planned tie-up with Sweden's Stena Line AB will be approved, is expected to report profit growth at its property, housing, cruise business and Australian operations.
Some analysts say a May 1 election will muddy the regulatory waters with a likely change of government.

The planned ferry merger with Stena was announced in October to pool resources in the battle against Anglo French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc/SA, but some analyts said they did not expect a joint venture -- and its financial benefits -- before the summer.
P&O's shares were trading at 621.5p, a loss of 8.5p on Friday afternoon.
